messages.subject: Person-level random effect
parts:
Hi,

I am a bit confused by syntax for adding a person-level random effect. Each person has two samples, so in an LME framework I would do something like 1|id. How do I do this in inla? fieldcode = person id. 

I tried:

resp <- "cortisol" # Response variable

covar <- c("age_binyr",# age bin
           "testosterone", # testosterone
           "age_binyr:testosterone"#interaction)

f1 <- as.formula(paste0(resp, " ~ ", # Response first
                          paste(covar, collapse = " + ") # Collapse the vector of covariates
))

m1  <- inla(cortisol ~ age_binyr + testosterone + age_binyr:testosterone,
               family = "gaussian", # Specify the family
               data = mydata2)

m2_re <- as.formula(paste0(resp, " ~ ",
                          paste(covar, collapse = " + "),
                          " +  f(fieldcode, model = 'iid')"))

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Person-level random effect
parts:
Hi Delaney,

I don't see any problems with that model definition; the f(fieldcode,
model="iid") component will give you a per-individual random effect.

Finn
